summary: Over a 14-day analysis period, CGM coverage was excellent (98.7%) with a mean glucose of 121.6 mg/dL and 86.0% Time in Range (70–180 mg/dL). However, Time Below Range (5.1%) exceeds clinical targets (<4.0%), driven by recurrent hypoglycemia clusters in the early evening (18:00–19:00 local, 15.3% TBR) and early night (00:00–03:00 local, 10–18% TBR). These lows consistently follow pronounced afternoon hyperglycemic spikes (13:00–17:00 local, up to 32.1% TAR). Because zero carbohydrates were logged over the 14 days, the system relies entirely on unannounced meal (UAM) SMB delivery. Delayed insulin delivery leads to sharp post-meal rises, which trigger aggressive Dynamic ISF SMB auto-dosing. Permissive safety limits (Max IOB = 25 U, Max Basal = 12 U/h) allow excessive insulin stacking, resulting in steep drops and rebound hypoglycemia. Fasting glucose from 04:00 to 08:00 local is stable (95%+ TIR), indicating underlying basal rates are well-tuned.

analysis_steps.findings: 14 days of high-density CGM data with 98.7% coverage (3,995 valid entries). Local time context BST (UTC+1). Full profile context available.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 entries out of 4,046 expected; 10 small gaps (largest 65.0 min). 655 insulin treatments (275.95 U total TDD ~19.7 U/day). Active profile active and authoritative.
data_gaps: Carbohydrate logging gap: zero carb entries recorded over the 14-day period.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall control is strong (86.0% TIR), but hypoglycemia risk (5.1% TBR) is elevated. Recurrent low clusters occur in early evening (18:00–19:00 local) and early night (00:00–03:00 local). Extreme minima reach 41–42 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hour 19 has 15.3% TBR (mean 105.4 mg/dL); local hour 01 has 18.5% TBR. Severe lows on Aug 13 (42 mg/dL), Aug 14 (41 mg/dL), Aug 21 (42 mg/dL). TAR spikes reach 32.1% at local hour 15.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight and early morning fasting basal segments (04:00–08:00 local) maintain excellent glucose stability in the absence of meal and correction insulin.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR from 04:00–08:00 local ranges between 95.2% and 98.7% with mean glucose 99.5–106.0 mg/dL. Current basal segments (00:00 0.6 U/h, 05:00 0.7 U/h, 06:00 0.8 U/h) hold glucose steady.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile ISF is 56 mg/dL/U and DIA is 10 h. Nominal settings appear adequate, but combined Dynamic ISF and UAM auto-dosing during high excursions significantly over-corrects hyperglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Correction windows show steep drops: Aug 14 16:20 UTC correction dropped glucose -178 mg/dL in 120m; Aug 19 15:55 UTC dropped -168 mg/dL in 120m. Dynamic ISF reduces active ISF down to 27.8 mg/dL/U during spikes.
data_gaps: Unannounced meals prevent isolated calculation of true CR versus timing delay.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled with smb_always_enabled=true and 3-minute interval. Automation functions as the primary meal bolus engine due to unannounced meals.
analysis_steps.evidence: Loop logs confirm frequent SMB micro-bolusing and UAM High Boost activations during afternoon spikes (e.g., Aug 19 15:55 UTC UAM High Boost delivered 1.6 U SMB at 262 mg/dL).

analysis_steps.findings: Max IOB (25 U) and Max Basal (12 U/h) safety limits are excessively permissive for an average TDD of ~19.7 U/day, permitting dangerous insulin stacking during high glucose deltas.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max IOB of 25 U represents >125% of Total Daily Dose. Scheduled basal max is 0.8 U/h, making Max Basal 12 U/h 15 times the baseline rate. Dynamic ISF factor is set to 70%.

analysis_steps.findings: Unannounced meals create an inherent insulin delivery lag, causing post-prandial hyperglycemia to peak 1–2 hours after eating before automated UAM SMBs catch up and over-correct.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hours 13:00–16:00 show consistent TAR increases peaking at 32.1% (hour 15, avg 162.8 mg/dL), followed immediately by high TBR at hours 18:00–19:00 (15.3% TBR). Zero carb entries logged.
data_gaps: Lack of logged carb intake timing and amounts.

analysis_steps.findings: Min 5m carb impact (8 mg/dL/5m) and meal max absorption (7 h) keep UAM carb models active for prolonged durations, keeping predicted glucose elevated and extending SMB delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: Protracted post-prandial elevations persist 3–5 hours post-meal, sustaining SMB micro-boluses until glucose drops rapidly into hypoglycemia.
data_gaps: Zero logged eCarb treatments in telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: The root cause of recurrent hypoglycemia is insulin stacking driven by unannounced meal lag, amplified by Dynamic ISF, and enabled by excessively high Max IOB / Max Basal caps. Underlying basal tuning is appropriate.
analysis_steps.evidence: Fasting TIR is 95%+. Hypo clusters occur exclusively downstream of high afternoon spikes. Max IOB (25 U) far exceeds TDD (19.7 U). Tighter automation safety limits combined with pre-meal announcements will resolve both high spikes and post-spike lows.

strengths: High CGM data completeness and continuity (98.7% coverage over 14 days).
Excellent baseline overnight fasting stability (04:00–08:00 TIR 95–98%), demonstrating accurate scheduled basal rates.
Overall Time in Range is strong at 86.0% with a mean glucose of 121.6 mg/dL.
issues: Recurrent hypoglycemia clusters in early evening (18:00–19:00 local, 15.3% TBR) and early night (00:00–03:00 local, up to 18.5% TBR).
Excessively high Max IOB (25 U) relative to Total Daily Dose (~19.7 U/day) and high Max Basal (12 U/h relative to 0.8 U/h max scheduled basal).
Absence of meal carb announcements forces complete reliance on UAM, introducing insulin lag, afternoon spikes (32.1% TAR), and subsequent insulin stacking.

recommendations.title: Reduce Max IOB and Max Basal safety limits to match Total Daily Dose
recommendations.description: Current Max IOB (25 U) exceeds average Total Daily Dose (~19.7 U/day), permitting extreme insulin stacking during post-meal spikes. Reducing Max IOB to 7.0 U (approx. 35% of TDD or 3.5x max daily basal) and Max Basal to 3.0 U/h creates an essential safety ceiling against severe automated over-dosing.

recommendations.title: Lower Dynamic ISF adjustment factor during high glucose spikes
recommendations.description: Dynamic ISF factor at 70% drops effective ISF down to 27.8 mg/dL/U during spikes >240 mg/dL. Reducing the adjustment factor to 50% tempers SMB aggressiveness during high deltas and reduces post-spike rebound lows.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Maintain active basal profile segments unchanged and verify fasting stability during zero-IOB windows.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Fasting glucose from 04:00 to 08:00 local demonstrates strong stability (95%+ TIR) on current basal rates (0.6–0.8 U/h). Post-prandial excursions and late hypoglycemia are driven by unannounced meal insulin lag and aggressive automated SMB delivery rather than baseline basal excess.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Confirm fast-state glucose stability overnight (00:00–06:00) on a night with no food or correction boluses after 19:00.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivery parameters are standard; limiting overall IOB through Max IOB is safer than restricting SMB delivery interval.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Max IOB of 25 U represents >125% of TDD (~19.7 U/day), creating severe hypoglycemia risk during high spikes. Reducing Max IOB to 7.0 U (~35% of TDD) and Max Basal to 3.0 U/h establishes a vital safety ceiling.
Dynamic ISF adjustment factor of 70% overly strengthens insulin delivery at high glucose (effective ISF 27.8 mg/dL/U), causing steep drops. Lowering factor to 50% moderates peak SMB aggressiveness.
Absorption parameters are suitable; meal announcements will optimize carb impact calculations naturally.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Announce main meals and bolus 10–15 minutes prior to eating (100% upfront bolus) to eliminate UAM detection lag. Retain UAM SMBs as a backup for unannounced snacks or minor carb underestimates.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Unannounced meals cause an inherent 30–60 minute lag in insulin action, resulting in afternoon hyperglycemia up to 293 mg/dL followed by automated over-dosing and evening lows (15.3% TBR). Pre-bolusing matches insulin peak with carbohydrate absorption.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log exact carb amounts and meal times for 3 consecutive days to evaluate true Carb Ratio (CR) accuracy during pre-bolused meals.

exceptions.suggestion: Deliver 50–70% of calculated meal insulin upfront and enter the remaining carbs as e-Carbs over a 2–4 hour duration.
exceptions.rationale: Prevents early post-meal hypoglycemia while providing sustained coverage for extended fat/protein absorption without triggering reactive UAM over-dosing.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Reduce Max IOB in AAPS settings from 25.0 U to 7.0 U, and Max Basal from 12.0 U/h to 3.0 U/h.
Step 2: Lower the Dynamic ISF adjustment factor from 70% to 50% in AAPS settings.
Step 3: Begin logging meal carbohydrate amounts and administering boluses 10–15 minutes before meals.
Step 4: Monitor glucose stability over 3–5 days, specifically evaluating whether early evening low clusters (18:00–19:00) resolve.
Step 5: Review CR accuracy once 3 days of clean meal bolus data are collected.
education: Unannounced meals force closed-loop algorithms to wait for rising sensor glucose before delivering insulin. This lag naturally causes higher post-meal peak glucose compared to pre-bolusing.

Max IOB serves as a crucial safety limit in automated insulin delivery. Setting Max IOB near or above total daily insulin requirement increases the risk of severe insulin stacking during persistent high glucose readings.

Dynamic ISF automatically increases insulin sensitivity strength as glucose rises above target. High adjustment percentages can cause over-correction when large carb absorption curves are still active.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change with their healthcare team.
Adjust safety settings (Max IOB and Max Basal) first before modifying profile parameters.
Make parameter changes one at a time and monitor sensor glucose closely for at least 48 hours following any adjustment.
